names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 aprilie, «Sfântul Mucenic Teodul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Θεόδουλος και Αγαθάπους», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 5 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Агатопод и Теодул“, with the rank words Св. муч. left off; they head the pair and belong to neither name. The heading gives the two forenames bare, with no epithet and no city — Thessalonica is in the body — so the bare forename is what the source gives, and two other folders already hold it.

Read out of the title on the name link behind his part of the line for 5 апреля ст. ст., name page 2232, «Феодул Солунский (Фессалоникийский), мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off and the city kept in both the forms the calendar prints. The day’s own line gives the forename in the genitive with his office, чтец, beside it. No folder holds this form or the bare «Феодул».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 апреля ст. ст. — «Мчч. Агафопода диакона, Феодула чтеца и иже с ними (ок. 303).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 aprilie — «Sfântul Mucenic Teodul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Θεόδουλος και Αγαθάπους»

attestations.note: The Greek calendar keeps the pair on 4 April, a day earlier than the Romanian 5 April this folder already records; the life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους». The page puts them «στα πρώτα χρόνια των διωγμών», in the first years of the persecutions, and gives no year, so no dates are recorded from it. It spells the companion's name Αγαθάπους in the day's line and Ἀγαθόπους and Άγαθάποδας in the life, and prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.04.2026 (5. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Агатопод и Теодул“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, one heading naming both men, **on the Romanian calendar's day and not the Greek one**, and the same man this folder holds: the reader of the church at Thessalonica, the younger of the two, drowned with his deacon. **A death of 303 was added where this folder had none**, said of the two together, and it is the only year any source read for this folder gives. New besides that: the chastity the entry sets against his companion's grey hairs; the two going to trial hand in hand crying that they were Christians; the imprisonment and starving; and **his appearance after death — „Св. Теодул се јави својим познаницима, као ангел светао, у белом оделу, и нареди им да све његово заостало имање разделе сиромасима“** — he appeared to his acquaintances as a shining angel, in white clothing, and told them to divide all the property he had left among the poor. **His grade has no slug here**: the entry calls him чтец, a reader, and this corpus's `types` vocabulary holds no word for it, so nothing was added and nothing was invented. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. The stored form Теодул folds with `theodulus-companion-of-pamphilus` and `theodulus-of-myropolis`, which hold the same bare form; the fold is recorded as deliberate.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinţilor Mucenici Teodul şi Agatopod, Glasul 4 (the page's «nesctricăciunii» is the reading printed there)

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received incorruptible crowns from thee, our God; for having thy strength they overcame the tormentors, and they broke also the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 5 April, of the two men together: „Ови дивни Христови војници чесно пострадаше у време цара Диоклецијана и солунског кнеза Фаустина, 303. године“ — in the time of the emperor Diocletian and of Faustinus, prince of Thessalonica, in the year 303. The year is printed flat and not as «about». It is the only year any source read for these two folders gives them: neither doxologia.ro's notice nor saint.gr's prints one, and the persecution of Diocletian they both name is consistent with it. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 303` reads in Russian and Greek.
